psalm.edition: Brian Walton, Biblia sacra polyglotta (London: Thomas Roycroft, 1657)
psalm.rights: 1657 source text public domain; Internet Archive scan item marked CC0 1.0 Universal.
psalm.review: Manually transcribed from the printed Syriac column, lower left, line 3; letters and vowels independently checked against an enlarged render. The printed terminal colon is replaced by full stops, and a response line break and bold markup are added for presentation. No letters or vowel signs changed.

alleluia.edition: The New Testament in Syriac, BFBS 1905; Digital Syriac Corpus
alleluia.credit: Syriac transcription by George A. Kiraz; TEI XML edition © James E. Walters, CC BY 4.0. The Syriac base text is public domain.
alleluia.sourceVerse: ܘܡܶܢ ܒ݁ܳܬ݂ܰܪ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܆ ܫܶܡܥܶܬ݂ ܩܳܠܳܐ ܪܰܒ݁ܳܐ ܕ݁ܟ݂ܶܢܫܶܐ̈ ܣܰܓ݁ܺܝܶܐܐ̈ ܒ݁ܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܕ݁ܳܐܡܪܺܝܢ ܆ ܗܰܠܶܠܽܘܝܰܐ . ܦ݁ܽܘܪܩܳܢܳܐ ܘܬ݂ܶܫܒ݁ܽܘܚܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܚܰܝܠܳܐ ܠܰܐܠܳܗܰܢ .

assembly: Prosary joins the separately sourced Psalm opening and Alleluia to the unchanged supplied gloriaPatri in each script. This is not a claim that Walton prints a Syriac Rosary formulary. Lent omits only Alleluia. The existing Erez-supplied basic prayers are not retranslated or replaced.
